venues.name: CC Atlanta
venues.narrative: **CCATL — Fri 9/18 (MOD JK).** Net $7,073 vs $6,682 target (106%); food $542; no events; comps $164 (2.3%); 225 guests / $31.44 avg. Sunny, upper 80s. (Form date mis-typed as 2026-04-03; matched by post time.) Slower start, picked up around 8–9pm, strong push at 10:30–11pm likely from guests leaving Shaky Knees in Piedmont Park. No barback tonight but back-of-house support kept things smooth — thanks Keyshawn. Sold a lot of Shorty services; effectively sold out for next Saturday evening. Guests stayed until close; everyone out by 2:30am. Kitchen: double-check classic dog condiment mods. Low on High Life ponies. No incident; no no-shows charged. Favorite moment: high-school friends came in for Shorty service and complimented the atmosphere and DJ. Entered by Daniel.

venues.name: CC Nashville
venues.narrative: **CCNSH — Fri 9/18 (MOD KK/MD/KE; Chef JMS).** Net $15,848 vs $11,905 target (133%) — bar $10,098 + Dairy Boy event upstairs $5,750; food $300; comps $48.30 (0.3%); ~363 guests / $27.82 avg (bar only, excludes event). Very hot. Fun Friday that tested a lot of new team members — several regulars out by happenstance, so the newest folks got to shine and held down the fort. Upstairs Dairy Boy event went smoothly; MD and KK kept the guest experience excellent and hosts were very pleased (note: no beers sold upstairs all night). Slow start at the main bar with Americanafest in town and a younger crowd in the area; picked up by 9pm as event guests trickled in and the usual crowd arrived; steady and fairly busy 9pm–midnight. Kitchen: slightly lower food sales with the festivities; JMS and DM supported the team elsewhere. Maintenance: cosmetic Well 1 tap handle; freezer water issue. No 86s. No incident; no no-shows charged. Favorite: regulars, teammates and neighboring-bar friends wishing KE a happy birthday all night. Entered by KE.

venues.name: D&C Denver
venues.narrative: **DVR — Fri 9/18 (AM Maggie S. + Josh; PM Carey + Lucas).** Net incl. events $25,283.77 vs $17,476 target (145%); DC/AM $1,648.77, D&C PM $13,639, Garden n/a (closed for wedding); non-event net $15,287.77; event net $9,996 (event food $4,000); total food incl. events $6,675; comps $4,222.48 (2.76% as reported — includes event); 402 guests (Tock) / ~$62.89 avg. (Form date typed 9/19; matched by post time and day-of-week.) AM: killer day with Heather Ramsey, busy throughout; second half of coffee order arrived — thank you Felix. PM: nice night that felt slow but stayed full all night; no Garden service due to the wedding; fully staffed floor made for smooth sailing. Kitchen: steady Friday for Rand and Ayu with Lucas holding down the event. Event: Funero wedding reception, 49 guests, 6–11pm in the Garden and 6A; Lucas' apps were crushed, Jake great on his first event, Madi/Travis/Justice worked well together, club DJ set; couple and friends thanked the team — thank you Kelly. Break make-up complete. No-shows charged. No incident. Favorite: smooth evening with a dialed-in staff and Maggie S. back. Entered by Carey.

venues.name: D&C East Village
venues.narrative: **EV — Fri 9/18 (MOD Kyler; Chef Steves).** Net $8,252 vs $7,825 target (105%); food $699; beverage $7,553; retail $0; no events; comps $96.34 (1.2%); 254 guests (Sevenrooms) / $32 avg. Crisp autumn evening. (Form dated 'Friday 9/19'; matched by post time — door notes say Friday 9/18.) Stagnant opening turn despite a 20-person line at open; healthier at 8pm with the strongest turn at 10pm. Plenty of whiskey drinkers gravitating to Paper Wasp. Smooth final hour with guests trickling out before last call; strong numbers, easygoing pacing. Top sellers: Burner Phone, Eight Limb Daiquiri / High Plains Drifter (tie), Cloudwalk / Long Time Caller (tie). Door (HP): strong start, flipped for an 8pm flow with no waitlist, then a list built from 8:45 — duos under an hour, 3–4 tops up to 2.5 hours; big 10pm turn packed the room; waitlist cleared at 1am, still mostly full at 1:15am. Notable guests: regular Cole, member Brett Stack, member Neela Minesinger celebrating parents' 30th anniversary, plus industry folks, returning tourists and a 21st birthday. One no-show (Anisha, 2 at 6pm) — no-shows charged. Menu count 19/19; breakage 4x DOF. Maintenance: ongoing leak downstairs by stairs. Entered by Sean.

venues.name: D&C Los Angeles
venues.narrative: **LA — Fri 9/18 (MOD Gigi + Julian + Joe + Josh + Angel + Saleh).** Net $12,217 vs $11,360 target (108%); food $2,226; Standing Room $3,191, Marquee $9,026; comps $410 (3.4% — Philip, Frank, birthdays, anniversaries, industry, investors, DNL); 297 guests / $41.13 avg (form typed $96.96, which doesn't reconcile with net ÷ guests; computed avg used). Very busy Friday: opened with 120 covers and a steady first hour with a good number of early walk-ins; bulk of reservations 8–10pm with lots of large parties. Gracy's first night live on the floor — she crushed it. Some interesting guests but the team kept everyone happy; both rooms completely full all night with a hefty waitlist of large parties; burned and turned all night. Marquee stayed full until last call with great vibes and a smooth ending. Kitchen: busy night, crushed it. No incident; no-shows charged. Favorite: Mike eating all the tater tots (per Ryan). Entered by Joe.

venues.name: D&C Washington DC
venues.narrative: **DC — Fri 9/18 (MOD Marcus / Josh).** Net incl. events $8,223.14 vs $8,584 target (96%); Marquee bar $7,528.24, Garden $871, total sales $8,399.24; food $866; no events; comps $176.10 (2.1%) + voids $25; 188 guests / ~$43.74 avg (form reported GCA $35.91 / CA $77.48). Nice weather. Marquee: great start with a healthy mix of reservations and walk-ins for the first 90 minutes, hard lull around 6pm for an hour, then steady for a couple of hours before tapering; pacing, communication and service tight all night; most guests one or two rounds before moving on, team pushed food and beverage including leftover batches from prior events (Negroni Week menu, bach event depletions). Soft close from midnight, last call at normal time. Garden: light start and light traffic throughout; cut a bartender ~9pm and used the Garden as Marquee overflow; last call 10:30pm and guests moved inside. Kitchen: steady, larger plates to bigger groups; fingerlings, tartare and bread & butter top sellers; kitchen close checked. Do better: clearing KDS, running food. Maintenance: curtains; hot water heater (hot water out twice); service well rinser sticking. No incident; no no-shows charged. Favorite: Elliot in for an after-work bev. Entered by Josh.

venues.name: Municipal Grand F&B
venues.narrative: **MG — Fri 9/18 (AM Franck/Justin + Lex; PM Justin/James + Marcus).** Net $10,845 vs $11,637 target (93%); Municipal Bar AM $3,864 (59 OpenTable guests), PM $6,536 (231 guests), Sun Club $894, Hot Eye $1,389; food $4,171; no events; comps $449 (4.1%); 290 guests / ~$37.40 avg. Beautiful and warm. AM: steady from lunch with the restaurant fairly full from 11am and a chaotic moment at the start of happy hour; no complaints — settling into busy season. PM: great evening with plenty of hands on deck; a lot going on around town so more subdued than hoped, could have handled more volume, but numbers were pretty good. Sun Club (Jack): got crazy after Aimee left — tons of food and drink orders 3:30–5pm, social-media group staying at the hotel had a blast; lots of margs and lemon drops, running low on Cointreau and citrus; through the first keg of Sauv Blanc, one keg of each wine left; busiest night up there in a long time. Hot Eye: slower Friday than usual with busy pops and long lulls; SCAD crowd and influencers; hotel guests returned for a second night. Kitchen: great night, no notes. Maintenance: stinky smell in THE — find the source. No incident. Favorite: sold ALL the burritos in THE. Entered by Alexis.

venues.name: D&C Seattle
venues.narrative: **SEA — Fri 9/18 (MOD Julian Abel / Curtis Hayes).** Net $12,794 vs $7,000 target (183%); food $1,752; comps $647 total incl. $152 shifties (5.1%); 252 covers / $50.77 avg. Another great day with lots of walk-ins. (Form typed 9/19 Saturday; matched by post time — notes describe Friday.) Closing staff called Friday an awesome night; a lot of one-and-dones; slower start than recently, which was a nice change. Family meal was had by all. Kitchen: Sfian killed it. Maintenance: a few items in Julian's canvas; need Auto-Chlor to replenish chemicals. Nothing 86'd. No incident; no no-shows charged. Favorite: Curtis showing Belle how to make a Queen's Park Swizzle. Entered by Julian Abel.
